heading: Give your customers' AI assistants a valet key.
lede: Poppy, the Personal Agent Protocol, is a new open standard. It lets a person's AI assistant work with your company, say who it is, and do only what that person allowed.

check.label: Is a site ready for Poppy?

columns.title: Today
columns.text: Assistants click through your pages or call your support line. You either block them, or let them sign in as the customer with full access. It's all or nothing.

columns.title: With Poppy
columns.text: You give assistants one front door. Each customer chooses what their assistant may do there: look things up, see their account, or make changes.

valetKey.heading: Think of a valet key
valetKey.text: A valet key starts the car but won't open the trunk or the glovebox. Poppy gives each assistant the same kind of key: enough for the job, and nothing more.

steps.heading: How it works, in three steps

picture.label: Three steps in one picture. One: an assistant walks up to a company's door, marked with its public file, poppy.json. Two: the assistant gets a key whose tag reads View orders. Three: inside the key's limits it can track an order, while closing the account stays outside them.

items.title: Put up a sign
items.caption: You publish one small file on your site. It tells assistants where to go and how customers sign in.

items.title: The assistant introduces itself
items.caption: It says who it is. If it needs the customer's account, the customer signs in, usually on your own page, and picks what it may do.

items.title: It works within the key
items.caption: It can check an order or start a return, but only within what the customer approved. You decide which assistants get in, and customers can disconnect them.

stands.heading: Where it stands
stands.text: Brand new, and still a draft. [Meta and Sierra announced Poppy](https://sierra.ai/blog/introducing-personal-agent-protocol) on October 6, 2026, with partners including Shopify, Stripe and Walmart. Almost no company supports it yet.
